pre-k.title: Pre-K
pre-k.description: Foundational sensory learning, phonemic awareness, visual patterns, and counting through play.

math.title: Early Math & Patterns
math.description: Counting 1 to 10, recognizing shapes, and sorting by color and size.

lessons.title: 1. Counting Colorful Shapes (1 to 5)
lessons.audioScript: Let's count together! One bright sun, two blue birds, three green apples, four red stars, and five friendly puppies.
lessons.summary: We count objects by pointing to each one and saying the numbers in order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5!
lessons.contentHtml:
Counting is like singing a song where every number has its special turn!

When we count, we touch or point to one item at a time. Let's count our fingers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5!

flashcards.front: How many fingers on one hand? 🖐️
What number comes after 2? 🔢

quiz.question: How many stars do you see: ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ?

options.feedback: Great job! 1, 2, 3 stars!
Let's count again together: 1, 2, 3!

ela.title: Phonics & Storytelling
ela.description: Letter sounds, rhyming words, and interactive story listening.

lessons.title: 1. The Letter Sounds Song (A, B, C)
lessons.audioScript: Every letter makes a special sound. A says 'ah' like Apple. B says 'buh' like Bear. C says 'kuh' like Cat.
lessons.summary: Letters are pictures of sounds that we use to build words.
lessons.contentHtml:
Letters are magical building blocks! When we put their sounds together, we make words.

• A: Ah-ah-Apple 🍎
• B: Buh-buh-Bear 🐻
• C: Kuh-kuh-Cat 🐱

flashcards.front: What sound does the letter A make? 🍎
What sound does the letter B make? 🐻

quiz.question: Which animal starts with the 'Buh' sound?

options.feedback: Yes! Bear starts with the letter B!
Cat starts with the 'Kuh' sound (C). Bear starts with B!

science.title: Exploring Nature
science.description: The five senses, weather, animals, and plant growth.

lessons.title: 1. Our 5 Senses Explorer
lessons.audioScript: We explore the world with our five senses: Seeing with our eyes, hearing with our ears, smelling with our nose, tasting with our tongue, and touching with our hands.
lessons.summary: Our 5 senses help our brain understand everything around us.
lessons.contentHtml:
Your body has 5 amazing explorer tools:

👀 Sight: Seeing colors and shapes.
👂 Hearing: Listening to music and birds.
👃 Smell: Smelling flowers and cookies.
👅 Taste: Tasting sweet berries.
✋ Touch: Feeling soft blankets.

flashcards.front: Which sense do we use to listen to music? 🎵
Which sense do we use to feel a fluffy puppy? 🐶

quiz.question: What part of your body do you use to smell a rose 🌹?

options.feedback: Correct! Our nose smells lovely flowers!
Ears are for listening. Our nose is for smelling!

social-studies.title: My Family & Helpers
social-studies.description: Community helpers, feelings, sharing, and friendship.

lessons.title: 1. Community Helpers Around Us
lessons.audioScript: Community helpers are friendly neighbors who help keep us safe and healthy, like firefighters, doctors, librarians, and teachers.
lessons.summary: Community helpers work together to make our neighborhood safe and happy.
lessons.contentHtml:
In every neighborhood, wonderful helpers work every day:

🚒 Firefighters: Keep our homes safe.
🩺 Doctors & Nurses: Help us feel better.
📚 Librarians: Help us find exciting books to read.

flashcards.front: Who drives a big red fire truck? 🚒
Who helps us learn at school? 🏫

quiz.question: Who helps you find books at the library?

options.feedback: Yes! Librarians love helping us find great stories!
Pilots fly planes in the sky! Librarians work in libraries.

kindergarten.title: Kindergarten
kindergarten.description: Early sight words, basic addition with visual objects, plant lifecycles, and community geography.

math.title: Math & Visual Adding
math.description: Adding with pictures, 2D and 3D shapes, and counting to 20.

lessons.title: 1. Adding with Visual Apples (1 + 2 = 3)
lessons.audioScript: If you have 1 red apple in your basket and a friend gives you 2 more apples, how many apples do you have altogether? Let's count: 1... 2, 3! That is addition.
lessons.summary: Addition means putting groups together to make a bigger total.
lessons.contentHtml:
Addition is joining groups together. We use the plus sign (+) to mean 'add together', and the equals sign (=) to show the total.

🍎 + 🍎 🍎 = 🍎 🍎 🍎 (1 + 2 = 3)

flashcards.front: What does the + sign mean?
What is 2 + 2?

quiz.question: If you have 2 toy cars and get 1 more car, how many do you have?

options.feedback: Awesome! 2 + 1 = 3 cars!
Let's count: 2 cars plus 1 more is 3 cars!

ela.title: Sight Words & Early Reading
ela.description: Dyslexia-friendly high-frequency sight words and sentence building.

lessons.title: 1. Friendly Sight Words: THE, AND, IS
lessons.audioScript: Sight words are words that appear everywhere in books. The more we recognize their shapes, the smoother our reading becomes.
lessons.summary: Sight words are common words like 'the', 'and', 'is' that we practice recognizing quickly.
lessons.contentHtml:
Here are 3 super-words you will see in almost every story:

• THE: 'The cat sat.'
• AND: 'Apples and bananas.'
• IS: 'The sun is warm.'

flashcards.front: Spell 'THE'
Spell 'AND'

options.feedback: Perfect! 'The sun is bright.'
Try 'is' -> 'The sun is bright.'

science.title: Plant Life & Sunlight
science.description: Seeds, water, sunlight, and the four seasons.

lessons.title: 1. How a Tiny Seed Grows
lessons.audioScript: A seed sleeps in the soil. When it gets warm sunlight and gentle water, it sprouts roots downward and green leaves upward toward the sky.
lessons.summary: Plants need soil, water, and warm sunshine to grow strong.
lessons.contentHtml:
Every giant sunflower begins as a tiny seed! To grow, seeds need three friendly helpers:

💧 Water: Gives the seed a drink.
☀️ Sunlight: Gives the leaves energy.
🌱 Soil & Nutrients: Gives the roots an anchor.

flashcards.front: What 3 things do seeds need to grow?
Which part grows down into the ground?

quiz.question: What gives plant leaves energy from the sky?

options.feedback: Correct! Sunlight gives plants energy to make food!
Plants need sunlight to grow healthy and green.

social-studies.title: Our World & Maps
social-studies.description: Simple map symbols, continents, and caring for our planet.

lessons.title: 1. What is a Map?
lessons.audioScript: A map is a bird's-eye drawing showing where places are located, like streets, parks, rivers, and mountains.
lessons.summary: Maps show where things are from above, helping us navigate and explore.
lessons.contentHtml: Imagine you are a soaring eagle looking down from the sky. You would see roofs of houses, winding blue rivers, and green parks. That top-down view is a map!

flashcards.front: What does blue color on a map usually represent?
What does a map help us do?

quiz.question: What color represents oceans on a map?

options.feedback: Yes! Blue represents rivers, lakes, and oceans.
Water is shown with blue on maps.

1st.title: 1st Grade
1st.description: Place values (tens and ones), decoding vowel teams, animal habitats, and community rules.

math.title: Math: Tens & Ones Place Values
math.description: Understanding 2-digit numbers with visual 10-bars and single units.

lessons.title: 1. Building Numbers with Tens and Ones
lessons.audioScript: When we count past 9, we bundle ten single ones together into a 10-bar. So the number 14 is one group of 10 plus 4 single units.
lessons.summary: Every 2-digit number is made of bundles of 10s and leftover 1s.
lessons.contentHtml:
Numbers have homes called Place Values. The number 25 means:

• 2 Tens: (10 + 10 = 20)
• 5 Ones: (1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5)
Total = 25!

flashcards.front: How many tens are in 30?
What is 1 ten and 7 ones?

quiz.question: What number is made of 2 tens and 3 ones?

options.feedback: Spot on! 2 tens (20) + 3 ones = 23.
2 tens and 3 ones makes 23 (32 would be 3 tens and 2 ones).

ela.title: ELA: Bossy E & Long Vowels
ela.description: The silent E rule, compound words, and reading with expression.

lessons.title: 1. The Magic Silent E Rule
lessons.audioScript: When the letter E sits at the end of a short word, it stays silent but tells the vowel before it to say its own name! Like 'hop' turning into 'hope'.
lessons.summary: Magic E makes the vowel say its long name: Cap becomes Cape, Pin becomes Pine.
lessons.contentHtml:
Silent E is like a quiet superhero. It does not make a sound, but gives the other vowel super strength:

• Cap (short a) ➔ Cape (long a)
• Kit (short i) ➔ Kite (long i)
• Hop (short o) ➔ Hope (long o)

flashcards.front: What does 'Rob' become with a Magic E?
What does 'Hat' become with a Magic E?

quiz.question: Add silent E to 'TUB'. What new word does it become?

options.feedback: Great job! Tub becomes Tube!
Add an E to the end: T-U-B-E (Tube)!

science.title: Science: Animal Habitats
science.description: Rainforests, deserts, arctic tundras, and oceans.

lessons.title: 1. Why Habitats Are Home
lessons.audioScript: A habitat is a natural home where an animal finds food, fresh water, and shelter. Polar bears thrive in the icy Arctic, while camels thrive in sandy deserts.
lessons.summary: Animals have special adaptations that fit their specific habitat.
lessons.contentHtml:
Animals live where their bodies are best suited to survive:

❄️ Arctic Tundra: Thick white fur keeps polar bears warm and camouflaged in snow.
🏜️ Desert: Camels can store energy and walk across hot sand.
🌊 Ocean: Dolphins and fish use fins to glide through water.

flashcards.front: What is a Habitat?
flashcards.back: A natural environment providing food, water, and shelter for living things.

flashcards.front: Where does a clownfish live?

quiz.question: Which animal lives in a cold, snowy Arctic habitat?

options.feedback: Correct! Polar bears have thick blubber and fur for the icy Arctic.
Camels live in warm, dry deserts.

social-studies.title: Social Studies: Community & Rules
social-studies.description: Why we have laws, fairness, and citizenship.

lessons.title: 1. Why Do We Have Rules and Laws?
lessons.audioScript: Rules help everyone stay safe and be treated fairly. Just like rules in a board game make sure everyone has fun playing together.
lessons.summary: Rules keep us safe, protect our belongings, and ensure fairness.
lessons.contentHtml:
Imagine playing a soccer game where players could use their hands, kick anywhere, and make up scores. It would be chaos!

Rules and laws exist so everyone can live, learn, and play together peacefully and safely.

flashcards.front: Why do schools have rules?
flashcards.back: To keep students safe and make sure everyone can learn happily.

flashcards.front: What does a green traffic light mean?

quiz.question: What is the primary reason for traffic safety rules?

options.text: To keep drivers and pedestrians safe
options.feedback: Exactly! Traffic rules prevent accidents and protect everyone.

options.text: To make cars go slower for no reason
options.feedback: Rules are created for safety and organization.

math.title: Math: Practical Financial & Calculus
math.description: Budgeting, compound interest, loans, and introductory derivatives.

lessons.title: 1. The 50/30/20 Visual Budgeting Method
lessons.audioScript: Budgeting doesn't have to be overwhelming numbers. Think of your income as three distinct buckets: Needs, Wants, and Future Savings.
lessons.summary: 50% Needs, 30% Wants, and 20% Savings create a balanced life budget without arithmetic stress.
lessons.contentHtml:
Adult finances are much easier when managed with visual systems. The 50/30/20 framework divides take-home pay into 3 clear priorities:

• 50% Needs: Rent, groceries, medication, utilities, and transport.
• 30% Wants: Hobbies, eating out, games, subscriptions.
• 20% Savings: Emergency fund and long-term security.

flashcards.front: What percentage is reserved for Needs?
Why is the 20% savings bucket critical?
flashcards.back: To build an emergency fund that protects you from sudden expenses.

quiz.question: Which expense belongs in the 50% Needs bucket?

options.feedback: Correct! Shelter and food are essential needs.
Gaming subscriptions belong in the 30% Wants bucket.

ela.title: ELA: Capstone Research & Synthesis
ela.description: Independent thesis writing, presentation skills, and media literacy.

science.title: Science: Astrophysics & Cosmology
science.description: Black holes, relativity, the expanding universe, and quantum concepts.

lessons.title: 1. Orbital Mechanics & Gravity
lessons.audioScript: Planets in orbit are essentially in constant free-fall around their star, where their forward momentum perfectly matches the downward pull of gravity.
lessons.summary: Orbits are the delicate balance between forward velocity and gravitational pull.
lessons.contentHtml: Gravity acts as the cosmic tether holding celestial bodies in place. The Sun holds 99.8% of the Solar System's mass, curving spacetime around it.

flashcards.front: What creates an orbit?
flashcards.back: The balance between forward speed and gravitational pull.

flashcards.front: How much mass does the Sun hold?
flashcards.back: Over 99.8% of the entire solar system's mass!

quiz.question: What keeps Earth from escaping into deep space?

options.feedback: Spot on! The Sun's intense gravity keeps Earth in orbit.
Gravity is the fundamental force responsible for planetary orbits.
